title: TaskingRequestRejected
description:
A tasking request was refused by tasking-api before entering the pipeline. Note this is a REJECTION, not an UNFULFILMENT: the request never became work. A request that was accepted and later lost the allocation gets planning.request.unfulfilled.v1 instead. Keeping the two distinct matters because they have completely different customer remedies — fix your input versus raise your bid.

Why this is an event at all, given that the caller already got a 4xx synchronously: the read model in plan-gateway needs the rejection for the customer's request history, and the operator needs rejection rates per reason as a metric. Publishing it is how those stay consistent with the write side.

request_id.description: Assigned even for rejected requests, so the customer has a stable handle to quote in support and so the rejection is addressable in the read model.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable rejection cause. A closed enum, not free text, because the frontend's 'why?' panel branches on it and dashboards aggregate by it. CONSTRAINTS_UNSATISFIABLE covers constraints that no configured sensor could ever meet — caught at ingress rather than wasting a feasibility sweep to discover it. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT means the key was reused with a different payload, which is a client bug and must not be silently treated as a replay.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the submitted body, e.g. /window/end. Lets the frontend highlight the offending field rather than showing a wall of text.

data.reason_detail: window.end is 2026-08-06T00:00:00Z, which is before the current time.
